subject: ADR-191: the session -- every snapshot carries a stamp, `since` answers what CHANGED instead of the snapshot, every act carries the same change against the snapshot the client planned it from, and the console keeps one door open between invocations
body: THE THIRD BLIND TRIAL'S ARITHMETIC WAS SECOND CALLS: read the snapshot, act, read the snapshot -- and four to six times each, throw the page away and run the whole plan again. Both are one missing thing: a conversation in which the second sentence may refer to the first. Every snapshot now carries a `stamp`, a version of the OBSERVATION beside ADR-188's version of the numbering; observe(since=<stamp>) answers the change and not the snapshot; every execute response carries that change against the last snapshot THIS SESSION WAS SERVED. On the collection sheet a pick answers in 2,021 bytes where the snapshot is 76,975, and a control whose only change is that it renumbered is reported as that one field moving -- which is only possible because ADR-188 gave it a name that does not move. The plugin says what identity means on its own snapshot (identity(): keys, noise); the gateway does the diffing, so the page, the organism, the lab, the fixture and the session target all diff alike. MCP takes the stamp in the resource URI and the diff rides every tools/call result -- the snapshot never did, which is exactly why every operator re-read after every act. blind_console --session keeps one door open between invocations. And a commandable control finally carries its value under SENSITIVE_READ, which the redaction line has promised since ADR-108 and without which the diff of an act that enters data said `nothing changed`. verify_contract 115 -> 143, verify_mcp 73 -> 89, verify_report 160 -> 179; mutate_contract 36 -> 56, mutate_report 104 -> 110. Protocol 1.7. No page and no task was edited.
